activities.summary: Sourced via web search on RockFi's growth and DG France appointment (2026-09-22); disqualified after confirming it is ORIAS/CIF-registered rather than AMF-authorised, and has already built its own back/middle-office tech. Recorded to avoid re-researching it as a lookalike asset/fund manager.

description: Fintech/network operator for private wealth advisors, created 2023, positioning itself as reinventing private asset management via a network of independent managers plus proprietary back- and middle-office technology. Registered at ORIAS as a Conseiller en Investissements Financiers (CIF) head-network (no. 23 004 556), member of Anacofi (an AMF-recognised professional association) - not itself an AMF-authorised portfolio management company or investment services provider. Present in 18 French cities, serves 1,000+ families, targeting EUR 1bn AUM by end-2026, monthly collection reportedly growing 20%+. Appointed Germain Michou-Tonning as Directeur General France in 2026 (also referenced elsewhere as Directeur des Operations) to lead structuring for that growth.

fit.disqualified_reason: RockFi is a CIF (financial investment adviser) network/fintech platform for independent wealth advisors, not itself an AMF-authorised asset manager, fund manager, bank or licensed family office - it coordinates advisors rather than running portfolios or funds on Gaia's kind of front-to-back system. It also states it has already built its own proprietary back- and middle-office technology, reducing appetite for a third-party platform. Recording so we do not re-surface it as a lookalike fund/asset manager lead.
fit.reasoning: Fit ~30/60: adjacent-segment credit only (10, a CIF advisor network/broker-like model rather than a direct asset manager, fund manager or licensed family office) + priority market France (15) + third-party money exists at the level of underlying advised clients but RockFi itself does not manage positions/funds directly + not AMF-authorised as an SGP/PSI, only ORIAS/CIF-registered via Anacofi (partial credit only). Trigger and access are secondary to the structural mismatch.
